slots.title: October jobs added 165K, double the forecast
slots.body:
October nonfarm payrolls: **165K** actual vs **65K** expected (prior **60K**).

Private payrolls: **159K** vs **64K** expected.

Unemployment rate: **4.1%** vs **4.2%** expected.

Average hourly earnings up **0.4%** month over month (est. **0.3%**) and **3.1%** year over year (est. **2.9%**).

Broader U-6 unemployment—includes discouraged workers and part-timers who want full-time work—printed **7.9%** vs **7.9%** expected **7.6%**.

U.S. indexes closed mixed after the release:

- $SPY context: S&P 500 **+0.3%** to **7,378.90**
- Nasdaq Composite **+1.1%** to **24,579.42**
- Dow Jones **-0.5%** to **51,285.73**

Volatility gauge VIX finished **-9.0%** at **25.64**.

How does a print this far above consensus square with the wage and U-6 lines on the same report?

slots.title: US session recap — Nov. 6, 2026
slots.body:
The October employment report set the tone: **165,000** jobs added vs **65,000** expected, unemployment **4.1%**, and average hourly earnings **+3.1%** year over year.
Manufacturing payrolls rose **19K**; the broader private sector added **159K** vs a **64K** consensus.

The S&P 500 closed up **0.3%** at **7,378.90** (range **7,369.55–7,444.20**).
The Nasdaq Composite gained **1.1%** to **24,579.42**.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped **0.5%** to **51,285.73**.
The Russell 2000 rose **0.9%** to **2,754.11**.

Nasdaq sector averages leaned toward defensive and cyclical areas: Healthcare **+2.0%**, Industrials **+1.7%**, Utilities **+1.6%**, Energy **+1.3%**.
Technology was the laggard at **-0.7%** on a sector-average basis despite many individual chip names finishing higher.

Semiconductor and AI-related equities led the risk-on slice of the tape. **$AMD** rose **11.0%** to **449.04**; **$INTC** **+7.7%** to **56.28**; **$TSM** **+6.3%** to **375.44**. **$TSLA** gained **4.2%** to **358.22**. **$CRM** fell **-3.9%** to **213.65**; **$NFLX** **-3.3%** to **63.41**.

Earnings tied to several large moves. **$MRNA** finished **+5.3%** at **254.19** after EPS **0.38** vs **-1.10** expected and revenue about **$1.31B** vs **$890M** estimated. **$HUM** **+5.3%** to **433.74** (EPS **-0.70** vs **-1.00** est.). **$VST** **+10.6%** to **124.80** (EPS **3.01** vs **2.98** est., revenue **$6.35B**). **$UI** **+15.3%** to **592.84** on a profit and sales beat. **$CHTR** **-6.2%** to **118.07** after EPS **-20.50** vs **+8.90** expected despite revenue above estimate. **$BAM**, **$BEN**, and **$ELAN** also reported; **$PAA** and **$PAGP** missed on EPS versus estimates.

Afternoon data added **Michigan consumer sentiment (Nov)** at **51** vs **48** expected (prior **48**).
Payrolls had already reshaped rate-path debate in headlines and commentary; the sentiment print arrived with the cash equity session largely settled.

Cross-asset moves were comparatively subdued.
The CBOE Volatility Index fell **9.0%** to **25.64**.
Gold futures slipped **-0.8%** to **4,079.60**.
Brent crude was roughly flat at **98.32**; the oil ETF **USO** ticked **+0.1%** to **148.41**.
The dollar proxy **UUP** rose **+0.7%** to **29.13**; **EUR/USD** was **-0.7%** at **1.11**. **Bitcoin** was little changed, **+0.1%** to **75,787.05**.

Overseas equity cues from the data set included the Nikkei **-6.0%**, FTSE **-1.0%**, Hang Seng **+2.4%**, and Germany exposure (**EWG**) **-2.7%**—mostly outside U.S. cash hours but part of the global backdrop traders carried into the week’s end.

Treasury snapshot (dated **2026-11-04** in the feed): **10-year** at **4.9%**, **2-year** at **4.6%**, **2s10s spread** **0.32**.
